messages:
support_l2: FYI — PaymentsCo reporting a regression in trace view: their request IDs show up but DB spans are missing intermittently for a 6min window after our 14:10 deploy. They provided one sample request id: rq-pay-20260315-7f4a.

customer_paymentsco: Seeing only frontend -> payments-api -> backend-proxy spans, DB calls to postgres never appear in trace timeline. Not in 'traceview', not in raw spans list. Happens ~14:12-14:18 UTC.

oliver: Thanks, is this every request or a subset? Any common headers?

customer_paymentsco: Subset. We think it correlates to requests proxied through our new gateway (v1.3) — we saw some dropped headers. Example raw headers we captured: 

```
GET /charge HTTP/1.1
Host: api.paymentsco.com
X-Request-ID: rq-pay-20260315-7f4a
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
X-Trace-Flags: 1
Forwarded: for=10.0.0.5;proto=https
```

but our gateway log shows it rewrote traceparent to a short id: `tp=short:abc` in the forwarder and then our agent attached spans with a different trace id.

maya: That sounds like header mangling at the gateway. Do we have logs from the payments-api side showing the received traceparent?

customer_paymentsco: Attached in the ticket — payments-api received `tp=short:abc` for these requests. We can share sanitized logs if needed.

eng-runtime-bot: Deploy notice — payments-api v2.4.1 rolled in us-east-1 at 2026-03-15T14:10:13Z (sha: d4f3a).

jonathan: If the gateway rewrites traceparent, our stitcher likely can't link spans by trace id. But request IDs should still stitch if present. Are the request IDs getting stripped or hashed?

support_l2: Customer says X-Request-ID was present end-to-end in their logs, but our console shows request_id mapping only for some traces. They provided a failing example where trace view shows a standalone frontend span with no linked DB spans even though request id exists in metadata.

oliver: Can we grep ingestion logs for rq-pay-20260315-7f4a? Try: `kubectl logs -n ingest -l app=ingest --since=30m | rg "rq-pay-20260315-7f4a" -n`

maya: Also check the span parent ids around that time. Hypothesis: gateway reassigns trace id and we get mixed KV cache keys so parent pointers are dropped. Run a quick query against spans index for that trace time window: `SELECT * FROM spans WHERE request_id='rq-pay-20260315-7f4a' ORDER BY ts LIMIT 100;`

jonathan: If KV prefix caching is used on the runtime, a sudden change in trace id format could make later spans look like orphaned entries and never get linked. We should search for unusual trace id lengths in the 14:10-14:20 window.

support_l2: I've asked PaymentsCo for sanitized logs and a short repro curl that hits the gateway + direct payments-api to compare headers. They replied with a curl that shows rewrite: 

```bash
curl -v -H "X-Request-ID: rq-pay-20260315-7f4a" https://gateway.paymentsco.com/charge
# response headers include: X-Forwarded-Trace: tp=short:abc
```

oliver: Can someone from infra check the gateway config for header rewriting rules in that rollout? @jonathan can you take a look at the proxy filter chain?

jonathan: On it. Quick remote check shows an envoy filter applied in the canary that normalizes trace headers into a `X-Forwarded-Trace` custom header. That would explain why the canonical `traceparent` gets lost for downstream services. Reverting rule for the canary nodes now.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated for gateway-canary group at 2026-03-15T14:22:03Z by jonathan.

maya: After rollback we should re-run ingestion reconciliation for the affected window and backfill links where possible. Support, can you ask customer for 3 example rq ids across the window so we can improve matching?

support_l2: Sent a request for three IDs (including rq-pay-20260315-7f4a). Also offered a short maintenance window to replay logs if they can.

customer_paymentsco: Thanks. We'll pull the other two IDs and confirm once rollback is observed. Appreciate the quick response. :thumbsup:

oliver: Action items: 1) Revert header rewriting (done), 2) Run span-link reconciliation job for 14:08-14:25 UTC, 3) Add a guard in runtime stitcher to fallback to X-Request-ID when traceparent missing/formats differ.

jonathan: I'll open a runtime PR to prefer Request-ID stitching if traceparent is malformed and add a small metric to catch short/unknown trace ids.

eng-runtime-bot: Created ticket INF-4821: "fallback stitch on request-id when traceparent malformed" assigned to eng-runtime.

support_l2: I'll keep this thread updated with customer replies and reconciliation results.

customer_paymentsco: Confirmed rollback observed at 14:23 UTC and we see DB spans reappearing for new requests. We'll validate the older window and let you know if we still need replay.

oliver: Good. If reconciliation backfill recovers historic links we'll close. If not, coordinate replay. Thanks everyone.
